key_insight: Vision-Language-Action models often ignore instructions and fall back on visual shortcuts learned from biased data; the paper identifies these "counterfactual failures" and shows how targeted evaluation and simple mitigation reduce vision-overrides of language.
problem_solved: VLAs can repeatedly execute visually frequent behaviors or pick commonly seen objects regardless of language intent, compromising instruction following and robustness. The paper diagnoses these failures systematically and provides methods to measure and reduce them.
method: Introduce a counterfactual evaluation protocol that tests instruction adherence by swapping scene elements or command targets to reveal vision-driven shortcuts.
Define metrics that quantify language override (how often vision-leaning actions contradict instructions) and analyze dataset biases driving failures.
Propose mitigation strategies (e.g., counterfactual data augmentation, bias-aware training objectives, and alignment regularizers) to strengthen language grounding in action policies.
impact: Provides practical diagnostics and fixes so practitioners can better evaluate VLA systems for instruction fidelity and robustness, improving safe and reliable robot behavior in real-world, ambiguous scenes.

paper_title: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs
paper_authors: Yu Fang, Yuchun Feng, Dong Jing, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang
